map.PNH 流式细胞术 (CD55/CD59) 检测器 使用指南: PNH Flow Cytometry (CD55/CD59) Detector User Guide
map.输入流式细胞术检测的 CD55、CD59 缺失细胞比例及荧光强度，评估 PNH: Enter the proportion of CD55 and CD59 deficient cells from flow cytometry together with fluorescence intensity to assess PNH clone size (mainly the granulocyte and monocyte populations), and interpret clone burden and thrombosis risk in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria alongside the clinical picture.
map.用 FLAER/粒细胞克隆大小评估 PNH 负荷（最可靠）: Use FLAER and the granulocyte clone size to assess PNH burden (most reliable)
map.按克隆分级（亚临床<1 / 小 1–10 / 中 10–50 / 大>50）定治: Set treatment indications by clone grade (subclinical <1 / small 1-10 / moderate 10-50 / large >50)
map.结合血栓史、溶血、合并 AA 给警示: Raise the alarm alongside thrombosis history, hemolysis and combined AA
map.：克隆分级：最大克隆（粒细胞系，FLAER 最灵敏）= I+II+III 型缺失: Clone grading: the largest clone (granulocyte lineage, FLAER most sensitive) = the proportion of type I + II + III deficient cells. Below 1% is subclinical, 1-10% small, 10-50% moderate and above 50% large. Red cell clones are often underestimated because of transfusion dilution, so use the granulocyte lineage; large clones carry high thrombosis risk and call for visceral vein thrombosis screening.
map.：例（粒细胞 CD59 缺失=30%、其余为 0、有溶血）：最大克隆=30% →: Example (granulocyte CD59 deficiency 30%, others 0, with hemolysis): largest clone 30% -> moderate clone (10-50%); hemolysis suggests monitoring LDH and iron metabolism. A clone above 50% with hemolysis or thrombosis history calls for a complement inhibitor such as eculizumab.
map.FLAER 比 CD55/CD59 好在哪？: Where Is FLAER Better Than CD55/CD59?
map.FLAER（荧光标记气单胞菌溶素）直接结合 GPI 锚，不受输血稀释、灵敏度高，: FLAER (fluorescent aerolysin) binds directly to the GPI anchor, is unaffected by transfusion dilution and is highly sensitive, making it the gold standard for detecting granulocyte PNH clones; traditional CD55/CD59 can still help but is easily affected by red cell transfusion.
map.通常不需补体抑制，重点看是否合并再生障碍性贫血（AA/PNH 综合征），每 3–: Usually no complement inhibitor is needed; focus on whether aplastic anemia is combined (AA/PNH syndrome), and recheck flow cytometry every 3 to 6 months to monitor clone change.
